narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Repertoire"**

One performer, seven staged productions of the same script. The content (name, title, tagline, experience, skills, projects, blog) never changes; a switch in the header restages it in one of seven complete visual worlds: Editorial (the default), Avant-garde, Engineer, Creative, Arcade, Terminal, and Tape. The system's personality is plural on purpose. Each world commits fully to its own register (the broadsheet, the dark gallery, the Internet-Draft read in a pager, the studio, the arcade cabinet, the shell session, and the punched teletype tape). None of them is a theme laid over a neutral base, because the neutral base does not exist.

Underneath, one skeleton carries all seven: a fixed translucent header, a full-viewport hero, and a single centered column of sections (About, Experience, Education, Skills, Projects, Contact) at medium density. A world declares nine semantic color tokens (page, raised, text, secondary text, accent, accent hover, border, card, card hover), two font slots, and two radii, and the shared sections re-skin themselves. Two accent-use tokens sit on top for every world: `--on-accent`, the text on an accent fill (the page color by default), and `--accent-text`, small text in the accent (the accent itself by default); a world overrides either only when its accent needs it, as Editorial and Engineer do. A world may add tokens of its own beside the nine when its material needs them (Terminal's prompt green and bright text, Tape's punched windows); they never leave that world. Every world stages its own Hero, Experience, and Skills; Editorial, Engineer, Terminal, and Tape also stage their own About and footer, and the last three their own Education, Projects, and Contact.

The aesthetic philosophy is restraint everywhere except the accent and the display type. Every world spends its accent on small, high-signal things: buttons, period labels, rules, hover and selection states. Display typography carries identity, except in Engineer, where one face at one size carries it and hierarchy comes from numbering, position, indent, and bold. Motion is one shared reveal grammar (fade and rise on scroll, once) plus a single signature per world, staged in the hero and in its curtain.
keyCharacteristics: Seven complete worlds, one content source, switched at runtime and persisted per visitor.
One accent per world, spent on interactive and labeling elements only; Terminal's prompt green is its one sanctioned second voice.
Display typography carries identity: monospace, typewriter, geometric sans, heavy grotesk, display grotesk, slab poster, or condensed caps.
Flat, border-defined surfaces in six worlds; Creative alone lifts with shadow.
Shared reveal motion (fade, 30px rise, 0.5s, once) with a signature per world, staged in the hero.
WebGL in one world only (Avant-garde's particle field), mounted only while that world is active and backed by a CSS fallback.
Candy stays on the cards: Arcade's candy colors are surfaces, never UI chrome.
Bilingual by construction: every text node renders both locales and CSS shows one.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Each world has exactly one accent and spends it on buttons, labels, rules, hover and selection states. Body copy, headings, and card surfaces never take the accent. Arcade's candy colors are surfaces with Cabinet Black text on them, never accents. Terminal's prompt green is the shell's own prompt colour, held to the prompt user, active periods, JSON values, and the email key; it never becomes a second link or hover colour.

rules.name: The Own Palette Rule
rules.body: A world uses only its own token set, world-only tokens included. No Candy Green in Engineer, no Creative shadow in Editorial, no Tape Orange in Editorial or Signal Orange in Tape, no prompt green outside the terminal.

rules.name: The Dark Text on Bright Accent Rule
rules.body: Text on an accent fill reads `--on-accent`; small text in the accent reads `--accent-text`. Lime, Gold, and Tape Orange are light accents, so their fills take the page color, the default (6.3:1 to 16:1); Terminal's green key takes Terminal Ground (7.45:1). Violet's own hero and filter fills take white (6.7:1), and Engineer sets `--on-accent` to white on Link Blue (6.70:1). Signal Orange measures 3.0:1 on Newsprint and 3.3:1 under white text, so Editorial sets `--on-accent` to Ink (5.2:1) and `--accent-text` to Signal Orange Ink (#bf3900, 4.5:1 or more on every Editorial surface); in Editorial, `.text-accent`, `hover:text-accent`, and `group-hover:text-accent` all render in it. Raw Signal Orange stays on rules, outlines, fills, and text at 24px and up, which opts in through `.text-accent-display`.

rules.name: The Reverse Video Rule (Engineer)
rules.body: Engineer has two fills and no others: the blue Email key and reverse video (Ink fill, Cool Paper text). Reverse video marks what a pager would highlight: standalone figures in the copy (`.rfc-mark`, split out by `src/lib/figures.ts`, like `less` search matches), the pinned status line, and its "(END)".

rules.name: The Window Ink Rule (Tape)
rules.body: Running copy sits in punched White windows in Tape Black ink. Orange never sets text inside a window (2.79:1); there it only underlines and rules. Orange text lives on the black ground.

rules.name: The Heading Slot Rule
rules.body: Headings in shared components never hardcode a family. They use the heading slot (`--font-heading`) so a world can swap the voice in one token. A world's own stylesheet (`src/styles/worlds/<world>.css`) may name its faces directly, because those classes never render outside it.

rules.name: The Loud Display, Quiet Body Rule
rules.body: Identity lives in the display size and face. Body and label sizes stay between 0.75rem and 1.125rem in every world, except Tape's condensed body at 1.1875rem and its 1.25rem skill rows, which set the same measure a regular face sets at 1rem.

rules.name: The One Size Rule (Engineer)
rules.body: Engineer sets everything in Courier Prime at the text size except the hero's name and role. Hierarchy is numbering, position, a 3ch indent, and bold, never size.

rules.name: The Same Bones Rule
rules.body: Section order, container widths, and the About, Education, Projects, and Contact structures stay shared by default. A world forks a section only when its identity needs it: every world forks Hero, Experience, and Skills; Editorial also stages its own About and footer (its own Contact was retired on 2026-10-11 at the user's request, so it uses the shared one); Engineer, Terminal, and Tape stage their own About, Education, Projects, Contact, and footer, plus their own section headings in Experience and Skills (since 2026-10-11, when the user decided to keep the worlds and differentiate them). A fork lives inside the shared section, so anchors stay unique: the shared markup carries `data-design-hide="<world> <world>"` (space-separated) and the world's version `data-design-show="<world>"`. A world's own extras (Engineer's seams and pager) sit in `HomePage.astro` behind `data-design-show`.

rules.name: The 896 Rule
rules.body: Section content lives in an 896px column. Only the header and the hero widen to 1152px. Engineer narrows the whole page, hero included, to a 72ch column, the width of a plain-text draft.

rules.name: The Two-Radius Rule
rules.body: A world declares exactly two radii, `--radius-card` and `--radius-btn`. Chips, tags, and filters borrow the button radius; containers borrow the card radius.

rules.name: The Holes Are Data Rule (Tape)
rules.body: Every punched strip encodes real text, one column per character in its ASCII bits (channel 1 at the bottom, the feed hole between channels 3 and 4), via `TapeStrip`. A blank leader carries feed holes only. Never draw random holes.

dos: Do declare a new world with the nine color tokens, two font slots, and two radii on its `[data-design]` selector (overriding `--on-accent` or `--accent-text` only if its accent misses 4.5:1, and adding world-only tokens only for its own material), register it in `src/data/designs.ts`, add its `design.<id>` name in both locales, and add it to the anti-FOUC allowlist and both visibility selector lists in `global.css`.
Do keep the accent on buttons, labels, rules, and states (The One Accent Rule), and set text on an accent fill with `text-on-accent`, never a hardcoded white or page color.

Do treat Signal Orange as a display color: rules, outlines, fills with Ink text, and text at 24px and up through `.text-accent-display`. Small orange text goes through `--accent-text` (Signal Orange Ink, #bf3900); raw Signal Orange measures 3.0:1 on Newsprint and 3.3:1 under white text.
Do keep Tape Orange off text inside a White window (2.79:1); set window copy in Tape Black ink and let orange underline or rule there (The Window Ink Rule).
Do resolve headings through the heading slot and body through the body slot in shared components; a world's own classes live in `src/styles/worlds/<world>.css` and may name its faces there.
Do render both locales in every text node behind `data-lang-show` so the language toggle never re-renders.
Do respect `prefers-reduced-motion`, and make new motion join the reveal grammar (fade, 30px rise, 0.5s, once) or the world's own signature.
Do fork a shared section only when a world's identity needs it, inside the shared section with `data-design-hide` / `data-design-show` (The Same Bones Rule).
Do carry state as a mark or a word as well as a colour (Tape's band and cross, Terminal's "●" and "Present", `aria-pressed`, `aria-expanded`).
Do mount a WebGL scene only while its world is active, calibrate a lighter phone build, and ship a CSS fallback, as Avant-garde does.
donts: Don't mix tokens across worlds. No candy surface in Engineer, no Creative shadow in Editorial, no prompt green outside Terminal, no Tape Orange outside Tape (The Own Palette Rule).
Don't fork content per world. Copy, data, order, and links come from `src/data` and `src/i18n` only; a world may restage them, never rewrite or reorder them.
Don't add a fill to Engineer beyond the Email key and reverse video, or a size beyond the text size and the hero title (The Reverse Video Rule, The One Size Rule).
Don't punch decorative noise into Tape: every strip encodes its text (The Holes Are Data Rule).
